Application Materials.content:
For your application you will need:
- Personal details
- Transcripts and certificates of any essential qualifications
- Referee details
- A personal statement (if applicable to your chosen course)
- Your Queen’s student ID if you are a current / former student
**If you have completed your qualification, you should upload your degree award certificate and degree transcript. If you have not yet completed your degree, please upload your transcript to show results to date.**
**International Applicants:** To make sure your application is processed in the fastest possible time, you must scan and upload the following supporting documents along with your application. We may not be able to make a decision on your application until we have received all your relevant documents. Please upload good quality scanned copies of the following:
- Degree transcripts for all completed periods of study (undergraduate level and above).
- If your degree is still in progress, you must provide a transcript of results achieved to date. This can be requested from your university.
- Copies of your official Degree/Diploma Certificates, for the qualification(s) you have already completed. These are the documents that confirm the level and title of your qualification(s), for example, Bachelor of Science in Mathematics.
- Certified translations if your original documents are not in English. If you do not have translations at the time of application, please forward them by email to [student@qub.ac.uk](mailto:intl.student@qub.ac.uk) when available.
- Applicants whose first language is not English will need to show evidence of an acceptable level of competency in the English language.
For all applications (Postgraduate Taught and Research), you must include the names and contact details of two referees, normally academics, who are familiar with your undergraduate and/or postgraduate studies. If you have taken a higher degree or postgraduate course recently one of your referees should be from that institution. If you have been away from higher education for some time, you may use an employer as one of your referees. You do not need to include reference letters with your application. These will be requested directly by the University if required. Please therefore ensure that you carefully enter the correct email addresses for your referees.
For taught postgraduate courses, we aim to decide on your application within two weeks if we have received copies of all the necessary supporting documents. For some courses, an interview, admissions test or the submission of written work may form part of the selection process.

Application Deadlines.content: Applicants are advised to apply as early as possible and ideally no later than **14th August 2026** for courses which commence in **late September**. In the event that any programme receives a high number of applications, the University reserves the right to close the application portal prior to the deadline stated on course finder.

Academic Requirements.content:
- Normally a **strong 2.2 honours degree or equivalent qualification acceptable to the University in any discipline**.
- Queen's welcomes applications from a diverse range of backgrounds and **may consider previous managerial work experience alongside lower academic qualifications**.
- For postgraduate taught entry generally, entry to graduate diploma or taught masters programmes usually requires either a **UK upper second-class (2:1) or lower second-class (2:2) undergraduate degree**. Some taught programmes will accept a **UK 2:2 undergraduate degree with a minimum of 55% or equivalent**; for most courses, the major subject or content of the Bachelor degree may also be considered.
- **China Mainland applicants:** should hold a good **four-year bachelor degree from a recognised, well ranked university** with an average grade of **at least 70-85%**.
| Type of institution | UK 2.1 Hons standard | UK 2.2 Hons with 55% standard | UK 2.2 Hons standard |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tier 1 | Final average 75% | Final average 72.5% | Final average 70% |
| Tier 2 | Final average 80% | Final average 77.5% | Final average 75% |
| Tier 3 | Final average 85% | Final average 82.5% | Final average 80% |
- **Tier 1:** Prestigious Universities (Double First Class Universities and Top 100 Academic Ranking of World Universities). **Tier 2:** Other Recognised Universities and Independent Colleges affiliated to a Tier 1 Institution (as defined by Queen's). **Tier 3:** Other Independent Colleges recognised by Ministry of Education and Self-Study Degrees.
- **China Mainland borderline cases:** for many postgraduate taught programmes which require a UK 2:1 standard, Chinese graduates will normally be accepted with a final average mark of **up to 2% below the condition stated in the official offer letter**, assuming performance in key modules is of an appropriate standard. Where the entry requirements are different, borderline cases will be considered at the discretion of the Academic Selector.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
Evidence of an **IELTS** score of **6.5**, with not less than **5.5 in any component**, or an equivalent qualification acceptable to the University is required. **Taken within the last 2 years.** International students wishing to apply to Queen's University Belfast, and for whom English is not their first language, must be able to demonstrate their proficiency in English. Non-EEA nationals must also satisfy UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) immigration requirements for English language for visa purposes. For more information see [www.qub.ac.uk/EnglishLanguageReqs](https://www.qub.ac.uk/EnglishLanguageReqs).
If you need to improve your English language skills before you enter this degree programme, [Queen's University Belfast International Study Centre](https://qubisc.com/en?utm_source=Queens_referral&utm_medium=website_content&utm_campaign=courses/postgraduate-taught/supply-chain-analytics-msc/&utm_term=INTO+Queen%27s+University+Belfast) offers English language courses including [Academic English](https://qubisc.com/en/courses/academic-english?utm_source=Queens_referral&utm_medium=website_content&utm_campaign=courses/postgraduate-taught/supply-chain-analytics-msc/&utm_term=Academic+English) and [Pre-sessional English](https://qubisc.com/en/courses/pre-sessional-english?utm_source=Queens_referral&utm_medium=website_content&utm_campaign=courses/postgraduate-taught/supply-chain-analytics-msc/&utm_term=Pre-sessional+English).

Program Overview.content:
The MSc Supply Chain and Analytics is a **one-year full-time** programme developed to equip students with the qualitative and quantitative skills and knowledge to effectively manage supply chains using AI and business analytics. The programme focuses on business analytics, digital technologies, AI, and supply chain management, with emphasis on tools, processes, and practices that organisations can use to improve the productivity, sustainability, and resilience of operations and supply chains.
Students develop capabilities to evaluate, manage, and improve operations and supply chain processes; analyse operations and make evidence-based decisions; design effective and sustainable supply chain strategies and processes; develop and manage relationships in global supply chains; manage supply chain risks; and improve resilience. The programme provides exposure to real-world business problems, professional connections with employers and alumni, a culturally diverse learning environment, and access to world-class facilities.
Typical careers include Purchasing Manager, Supply Chain Manager, Operations Manager, Logistics Manager, Business Analysts, and Consultants.
- **Industry links:** The Supply Chain and Analytics Capstone is a final semester module that combines learning from across the degree and includes a dynamic online simulation where students work in teams to develop the global strategy of a firm in a game-based scenario. Capstone projects are applied practical projects where students work with real-world organisations to generate solutions to complex challenges.
- **Capstone pathways:** Students can choose from a Consultancy-Based Dissertation, Analytical Problem-Solving Dissertation, or Internship-Based Dissertation.
- **Career development:** A module on Developing Careers and Employability Skills is dedicated to enhancing students’ employability. Employer insights, networking circles, LinkedIn workshops, and job talks are embedded throughout the programme.
- **Student experience:** The programme focuses on how global managers and organisations navigate grand challenges and megatrends, including artificial intelligence, data analytics, sustainability, geopolitical instability, innovation, ethics, and doing business in emerging markets.
MSc Supply Chain and Analytics is structured across **3 semesters**. Students who successfully complete eight taught modules (120 CATS) and a Supply Chain and Analytics Capstone module in semester 3 are awarded an MSc in Supply Chain and Analytics. Exit qualifications are also available: a Postgraduate Diploma after 120 CATS from taught modules or a Postgraduate Certificate after 60 CATS from taught modules.
Students take seven core modules and choose one optional module, then complete a final capstone dissertation. The modules cover key knowledge and skills in operations and supply chain management, business analytics, and AI. Semester 1 provides knowledge of Business Analytics and AI; Semester 2 focuses on more specialised areas of supply chain management, including digitalisation, sustainability, and advanced analytics skills; Semester 3 is centred on the Capstone Dissertation, where students integrate supply chain management with AI and business analytics techniques and apply skills to real-world business scenarios.
People teaching the programme include [Dr Byron Graham](https://pure.qub.ac.uk/en/persons/byron-graham), Reader in Business Analytics; [Dr Rohit Nishant](https://pure.qub.ac.uk/en/persons/rohit-nishant), Professor of Information Systems; and [Prof. Min Zhang](https://pure.qub.ac.uk/en/persons/min-zhang), Professor in Operations Management and Business Analytics.
For semesters 1 and 2, students have 4 classes per week, all 3 hours long. Classes are delivered as a mix of seminars, lectures and workshops, using case studies, software demonstrations, practical workshops, role plays, groupwork, scenario discussions and organisation visits. Semester 3 is structured around independent and applied learning through capstone projects; students are assigned dedicated academic support and company mentors where relevant.
Assessments are applied and practical in focus, encouraging students to produce actionable recommendations for real-world scenarios and problems. Assessment types include presentations, reports, podcasts, game-based simulations, analytics practicals, teamwork and business plans.
Course location: [Queen's Business School](https://www.qub.ac.uk/schools/queens-business-school/). Queen’s Business School includes a 6,000 square metre building with digital infrastructure for media lecture capture, TED Talk provision and collaborative breakout sessions, a 250-seat tiered educational space, 120-seat Harvard style lecture theatre, 150-seat computer laboratory, breakout study spaces, FinTrU Trading Room, café, and Business Engagement and Employability Hub.

Curriculum.content:
Attendance: **1 year (Full-time)**. Course location: [Queen's Business School](https://www.qub.ac.uk/schools/queens-business-school/).
MSc Supply Chain and Analytics is a one-year programme structured across **3 semesters**. Students who successfully complete **eight taught modules (120 CATS)** and a **Supply Chain and Analytics Capstone module** in semester 3 are awarded an MSc in Supply Chain and Analytics. Exit qualifications are also available: students may exit with a Postgraduate Diploma by successfully completing **120 CATS** from taught modules or a Postgraduate Certificate by successfully completing **60 CATS** from taught modules.
Students on the programme will take **seven core modules** and will get to choose **one optional module** (eight modules in total at **15 CATS**). They will also complete a final capstone dissertation.
- **Semester 1:** Statistics for Business; Operations Analytics; Gen AI and Business Intelligence; Design Thinking with AI.
- **Semester 2:** Data Driven Decision Making; Digital Supply Chain Management; Supply Chain Sustainability; and one optional module from **Cybersecurity and Digital Risk Management** or **Emerging Technologies for Business**.
- **Semester 3:** The Capstone Dissertation module is the culmination of the MSc Supply Chain Analytics programme, allowing students to apply skills and knowledge from the taught modules to real-world business scenarios and propose viable and realistic solutions to an organisational or societal challenge.
The Supply Chain and Analytics Capstone is a final semester module that fosters capstone thinking and combines learnings from across the degree. It involves a dynamic online simulation where students work in teams to develop the global strategy of a firm in a game-based scenario. Capstone Projects are applied practical projects where students work with real-world organisations to generate solutions to complex challenges. There are **3 pathways** to choose from:
- **Consultancy-Based Dissertation:** engaging directly with an organisation to identify opportunities where supply chain analytics can be strategically implemented.
- **Analytical Problem-Solving Dissertation:** addressing a clearly defined organisational or societal problem through supply chain analytics techniques.
- **Internship-Based Dissertation:** designed for students undertaking an internship, where they critically analyse the ways in which the host organisation deploys supply chain analytics solutions to enhance its competitive position or resolve challenges.
For semesters 1 and 2, students will have **4 classes per week**, all **3 hours long**. Classes will be delivered as a mix of seminars, lectures and workshops. Semester 3 is structured around independent and applied learning through the capstone projects where students choose between different pathways.

Financial Aid.content:
**Scholarships of £6000 available exclusively for outstanding international applicants studying postgraduate taught programmes at Queen’s Business School in the academic year 2026/27.**
- Applicants must hold an offer to study a postgraduate taught programme at Queen’s Business School. **No application necessary.** If eligible, confirmation of your award will be issued with your offer.
- The **Queen’s Business School Scholarship** is available only to new students who hold an offer for a place on a **full-time postgraduate taught programme at the Queen’s Business School**, starting in the academic year 2026/27, and who have met any academic and language conditions attached to their offer before commencement of study.
- Students must be classified as international fee-paying students paying the full international tuition fee rate. Students paying NI, ROI, EU or GB fees are not eligible.
- The discount is awarded for the first year of study only and is deducted from **gross** tuition fees upon enrolment.
- Students must be self-funded, i.e. the tuition fees are being paid by yourself or your parents at the full international tuition fee rate.
- If you are in receipt of funding from an external sponsorship body such as Government, a charity or a private organisation, you will not be eligible for a Queen’s Business School Scholarship 2026/27.
- International scholarships cannot be used in conjunction with any other University tuition fee scholarship. Where **eligible**, students can use their scholarship in conjunction with the Early Confirmation Award or the ISC Scholarship.
- The University is unable to consider requests for increased and/or further funding. The amount of scholarship offered is non-negotiable.
[Terms and Conditions](https://www.qub.ac.uk/Study/international-students/international-scholarships/terms-and-conditions/)

Multiple Applications.content:
After you have entered the core details about yourself and your academic background, you can apply for one or multiple courses.
If you have applied for and been offered a place on more than one programme of study, you must indicate whether you wish to accept or decline the offer against each programme. Given that your final programme choice may be dependent on funding and/or other factors, you may initially decide to accept more than one offer of a place.

Deferral Admission Policy.content: Applications for deferred entry may be permitted. However, in considering requests for deferred entry it will be necessary to consider if the course will be offered in a subsequent year or, in the case of research, the research project and/or intended supervisor is available in a subsequent year. Requests will be considered on an individual basis, particularly in relation to non-UK/Irish applicants who may have experienced delays in obtaining an entry visa in time to commence their studies. Applications for deferral of University administered funding are not permitted.

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
- To accept or decline an offer, applicants should reply online through the [Queen's Portal](https://go.qub.ac.uk/pgapply), ideally within 14 days from receipt of the offer letter, even if they have not met the conditions of the offer yet.
- If an offer is conditional upon completion of a degree or other qualification, such as an English language examination, applicants must upload a scanned copy of their official examination results through the Queen's Portal.
- To upgrade from conditional to unconditional offer holder, conditional offer holders should upload scanned copies of their final transcript and degree award certificate, along with their English language qualification if appropriate, to the [Queen's Portal](https://go.qub.ac.uk/pgapply). Where applicable, confirmation of qualifications must be officially translated into English.
- Applicants should submit results even if they have not exactly met the academic condition(s) of their offer, as it may be possible to exercise some flexibility if places are available.
- For applicants who require a CAS, the tuition fee deposit must be paid before a CAS can be issued. CAS details will only be issued by the University to those who have accepted unconditional offers and paid the relevant deposits for Postgraduate Taught Programmes.
- Queen’s University Belfast International Study Centre offers English Language courses which may assist students to meet the required standard of English language to be eligible for entry to degree programmes, including [English for University Study](https://qubisc.com/en/courses/academic-english) and [Pre-sessional English](https://qubisc.com/en/search?facet-StudyLevel=%22English%20Language%22&facet-ProgramGroups=%22Pre-sessional%20English%22).
- Pre-sessional English is available for students doing a pre-sessional English course prior to the start of their degree programme. Start dates are **Mon 15 June 2026–Fri 21 August 2026 (10 weeks)** and **Tues 15 July 2026–Fri 21 August 2026 (6 weeks)**. Course length is **6 or 10 weeks**, class hours are **20 hours per week**, age requirement is **17 years and above**, and the academic entry requirement is that the student must hold an offer of a place on a degree programme at Queen’s University Belfast.
